exposure: Obstetric factors (preterm birth, post-term birth, complications during pregnancy, induction of labor, augmentation of labor, instrumental birth, planned cesarean section, emergency cesarean section)
cohort: 1414 women who gave birth across all birth settings in Flanders, Belgium, between 2013 and 2018
finding: Certain obstetric factors such as having a straightforward pregnancy without complications, a physiological onset of labor at term without the need for augmentation, and giving birth vaginally (without instrument) have shown a positive impact on women's reported birth experiences.
mod_finding: Women were more likely to report a better birth experience when birth took place at home or in a midwifery unit and when the main care provider was a midwife.
